merger_name: Wesfarmers and Built Group - Built Living Joint Venture

anzsic_codes.name: Pharmaceutical, Cosmetic and Toiletry Goods Retailing

merger_description:
Wesfarmers Limited (**Wesfarmers**) and Built Group Holdings Limited (**Built Group**) propose to establish an incorporated joint venture called Built Living Holdings Pty Limited (**Built Living**).

Built Living will establish advanced manufacturing facilities for the development of prefabricated residential apartment buildings on a national basis.

Wesfarmers is an ASX-listed diversified company with a broad portfolio spanning retail (including home improvement, general merchandise, office supplies and health), industrials and chemicals, resources, and data‑enabled businesses.  Key brands include Kmart, Target, Officeworks, Wesfarmers Health (which operates the Priceline brand), and Bunnings Warehouse.

Built Group is a privately held Australian construction and development group headquartered in Sydney, operating primarily in the commercial and industrial building construction sector. It provides end‑to‑end contracting services including construction, partnering with public and private clients to deliver large‑scale building and infrastructure projects across sectors such as commercial, residential, health, education and government.

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and information from third partes.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• There are no material horizontal overlaps between Wesfarmers
and Built Group.
• Bunnings Warehouse would be unlikely to have the ability to
foreclose rival suppliers of residential construction inputs by
fully or partly restricting their supply of competing inputs to Built
Living, given that there are multiple alternative acquirers of those
inputs.
• Built Group would be unlikely to have the ability to foreclose rival
suppliers of residential construction services by fully or partly
restricting their access to prefabricated residential construction
products from Built Living, given that rivals would be able to
continue competing effectively using on-site construction
methods and existing residential construction inputs.
